terms.comment: Cicero’s word, in the sense of the Academic philosophers: how likely or believable a thing is. The mathematicians kept it for probability as a measure. For “probably, in all probability” in speech, see probably (opīnor, vērī simile est).

evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.107: ipsam vērī similitūdinem … sequī
terms.comment: Often written as one word, vērīsimilitūdō; the adjective is vērī similis, likely.

phrases.latin: quodcumque nostrōs animōs probābilitāte percussit, id dīcimus
phrases.english: whatever has struck our minds as probable, that is what we say

sources: Lewis & Short: probabilitas · Lewis & Short: verus · Lewis & Short: similitudo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. probability.
Cicero, Lucullus (Ac. 2) 107 and Tusculans 5.33, checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
